beats.narration_text: Bonjour — this is Liam, in for Divyank. You've built quizzes and flashcards from your chapters, but none of it means anything to a student until they can actually open it on a Monday morning. This chapter turns the book into a course package — and checks that the course a student sees still matches the plan you signed.

beats.act: Act I — What You're Actually Exporting
beats.narration_text: Canvas has its own native course format. So does Moodle. So does Blackboard. A course package built to a shared standard runs on all of them — one track gauge, not three incompatible ones.

shot.prompt: real archival photo of narrow and standard gauge railway track side by side -- illustrative of a shared standard many systems can run on, not a literal depiction. Already sourced, see media/A1-1.source.txt

show.event: treated plate; slow push across the frame
serif label lands: 'one shared gauge, not three'

beats.act: Act I — What You're Actually Exporting
beats.narration_text: Build straight to Canvas's own A-P-I, and the course only ever lives in Canvas. Build to Common Cartridge instead, and Canvas becomes one of several places the exact same package can land.

show.event: question card: 'Canvas-only, or an open standard?'
two outcomes land

branches.detail: works today, locked to one platform
branches.fix: breaks if you ever leave Canvas

branches.label: Common Cartridge
branches.fix: Canvas is a destination, not a dependency

beats.act: Act II — One Command, One Path
beats.narration_text: One production line, run correctly, turns out the same kind of part every time. That's the whole design goal of this build step — one path in, one shape out, no matter which chapter set goes through it.

shot.prompt: real archival WWII-era photo of a production line manufacturing engine parts, Rolls Royce factory 1942 (IWM, public domain) -- illustrative of one repeatable build process, not a literal depiction. Already sourced, see media/A2-1.source.txt

show.event: treated plate; slow push across the frame
serif label lands: 'one line, the same shape, every time'

beats.act: Act II — One Command, One Path
beats.narration_text: Feed the same package into two different systems, and nothing about it changes to fit either one. The modules, the pages, the quizzes — they arrive the same, because the format never asked which platform it was headed for.

show.event: two tracks diverge: Canvas import, Moodle import

beats.act: Act III — Import, and the Silent Failure
beats.narration_text: An import can finish without a single error and still hand you an empty room — a course that looks complete from the upload screen, with nothing behind its own doors.

shot.prompt: real photo of an empty apartment room, bare walls and windows -- illustrative of something that looks intact from outside but is empty inside, not a literal depiction. Already sourced, see media/A3-1.source.txt

show.event: treated plate; slow push across the frame
serif label lands: 'looks complete. nothing's behind it.'

beats.act: Act III — Import, and the Silent Failure
beats.narration_text: An import that throws no error can still fail completely. If the manifest never actually linked its resources, the course imports — and shows you nothing. No error message tells you which one just happened.

branches.label: Course looks empty
branches.detail: resources never got linked in the manifest
branches.fix: failed silently, with no error at all

resolver.label: No error isn't the same as success
resolver.detail: only opening the course tells you which one happened

beats.act: Act IV — Order Is an Argument
beats.narration_text: In the chapter's own worked example, the import landed its modules alphabetically — Offers ahead of Foundations. Nothing was missing. Everything was just in the wrong order, and for a course, wrong order is the same failure as missing content.

show.event: two tracks diverge: alphabetical import, signed-order import

tracks.outcome: establish, build, apply — matches the plan

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Common Cartridge packages a course as a ZIP plus an X-M-L manifest — a shared standard, not a Canvas-specific format, importable by Canvas, Moodle, Blackboard, and more. One command, one path: build-canvas-dot-s-h wraps build-imscc-standard-dot-p-y, so every target builds the same shape, and the package itself is never a black box. An import can finish without error and still fail — if the manifest never linked its resources, the course looks populated or looks empty, and only opening it tells you which. And module order carries real pedagogy: the only reliable check is against the signed plan, architecture-dot-m-d, not memory — a course imported alphabetically can look complete and still be wrong.
